questions.question: Stereopsis is a feature associated with the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** eye.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The ability to see in **three dimensions—length, width, and depth**—is known as **stereopsis.**
 
• It enables a person to determine **how far away or close** an object is from them.
 
• Many different **visual inputs**, referred to as** depth cues,** are the source of depth perception.
 
• These depth cues might be **monocular (one eye) or binocular (two eyes).**
 
• Because the eyes are somewhat offset on the head, each eye receives a separate image, leading to **binocular vision (left and right eyes).**
 
• The term** "horizontal disparities"** or, more generally, **"binocular disparities" **is used to describe these spatial variances.
 
• The** visual cortex of the brain** processes disparities to produce **depth perception.**
 
• While **binocular disparities** are naturally present when viewing a **real three-dimensional scene** with two eyes, they can also be simulated by **artificially **presenting two different images separately to each eye using a** method called stereoscopy.**
 
• In these circumstances, the perception of depth is also known as **"stereoscopic depth." **

questions.question: Why can you not see objects in a dim lit room when you come from a brightly lit room?

options.text: The iris dilates the eye lens to allow less light to enter the eye.
The iris contracts the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.
The vitreous humour dilates the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.
The cornea contracts the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The iris contracts the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When we move from a** brightly lit room to a dimly lit room,** our eyes take some time to **adjust** to the change in lighting.
 
• This is because the** iris**, which controls the amount of light entering the eye, needs to** adjust to the new** lighting conditions.
 
• This helps to improve the **clarity of the image** that is formed on the retina.
 
• Dilation of the eye lens actually allows more** light to enter the eye**, and so this would not help in a dimly lit room.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iris:**

 
 
• The iris is a** circular muscle** in the eye that **controls the size **of the pupil and the **amount of light entering** the eye.
 
• It is responsible for adjusting the amount of light that enters the eye based on the** lighting conditions.**
 
 
 
• **Pupil: **
 
 
• **​**The pupil is the **black circular opening **in the center of the iris that allows light to enter the eye.
 
• Its size is **controlled by the iris**, which adjusts it based on the amount of light available.
 
 
 
• **Vitreous humour:**
 
 
• The vitreous humour is a **gel-like substance t**hat fills the eye and helps to maintain its shape.
 
• It does** not have any control** over the amount of light entering the eye.
 
 
 
• **Cornea:**
 
 
• The cornea is a **transparent layer** at the front of the eye that helps to focus light onto the retina.
 
• It does not have any control over the amount of** light entering the eye.**

questions.question: Select the correct statement.

options.text: The pyramid of energy is always upright.
The pyramid of biomass is always inverted.
The pyramid of mass is always upright.
The pyramid of number is always upright.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The pyramid of energy is always upright**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A pyramid of biomass is a graphical representation that shows the population at each level of the food chain.
 
• Producers occupy the base with the highest biomass.
 
• The relationship between numbers, biomass, energy, or bio productivity of an ecosystem can be represented by a pyramid known as the ecological pyramid.
 
• The trophic level is the place that a living organism occupies in a food chain.
 
• In a biomass pyramid, producers are at the base, followed by herbivores and then carnivores at the top.
 
• The pyramid of biomass shows the flow of energy from producers to consumers.
 
• 10 percent of the energy gets transferred to the next trophic level and the rest is either utilized for metabolic processes or excreted out.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carnivores that eat herbivores are called secondary consumers.
 
• A separate trophic level, the decomposers or transformers, consists of organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead organisms and waste materials into nutrients usable by the producers.
 
• Primary consumers make up the second trophic level. They are also called herbivores.

questions.question: Which cell organelles are known as the cell's post office?
questions.solution:

• It **modifies, sorts, and packages** the molecules in **vesicles** and sends them to their intended destinations.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is composed of stacks of flattened membranous sacs called** cisternae,** which are responsible for carrying out the aforementioned functions.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is present in **eukaryotic cells**, which include animal and plant cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The nucleus** is known as the control center of the cell, as it contains** genetic material (DNA).**

 
 
• It is responsible for regulating **cell growth, division, and metabolism.**
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes **are responsible for synthesizing proteins in the cell,
 
 
• They are either free in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **endoplasmic reticulum.**
 
 
 
• **Plastids** are organelles found only in** plant cells** and are responsible for functions such as** photosynthesis, storage, and pigment synthesis**.
 
 
• Plastids include** chloroplasts, chromoplasts, and leucoplasts.**

questions.question: Which of the following is an organic impurity in sewage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Human faeces.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Human faeces are an organic impurity commonly found in sewage.
 
• Faecal matter is rich in organic matter and contains various bacteria, pathogens, and undigested food particles.
 
• The presence of human faeces in sewage poses a risk to public health due to the potential transmission of diseases and contamination of water sources.
 
• Proper sewage treatment processes are necessary to effectively manage and eliminate human faeces to prevent environmental and health hazards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phosphates:**

 
 
• Phosphates are** inorganic compounds** that can be found in sewage as an inorganic impurity.
 
• Phosphates mainly come from** detergents, fertilizers, and human waste** that enter the sewage system.
 
• Excessive levels of phosphates in sewage can contribute to** water pollution and eutrophication** when released into natural water bodies.
 
• **Controlling and reducing the phosphate levels** in sewage is important for environmental protection and maintaining water quality.
 
 
 
• **Nitrates:**
 
 
• Nitrates are inorganic compounds that can be present in sewage as an** inorganic impurity.**
 
• Nitrates can originate from various sources, including **agricultural runoff, industrial waste, and domestic sewage.**
 
• Elevated levels of nitrates in sewage can lead to water pollution and pose a **risk to human health**, especially when they contaminate drinking water sources.
 
 
 
• **Metals:**
 
 
• Metals, such as** lead, mercury, cadmium, and copper, **can be present in sewage as** inorganic impurities.**
 
• These metals can originate from various sources, including** industrial discharges, domestic waste, and runoff from metal-contaminated areas.**
 
• Elevated levels of metals in sewage can have detrimental effects on the environment and human health.
 
• Effective sewage treatment processes, including filtration and sedimentation, are employed to remove or reduce metal impurities in sewage before it is discharged or reused.

questions.question: Who breaks down waste into smaller particles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**detritivores.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Detritivores** are the organisms that **break down waste** into **smaller particles.**
 
• They are also known as **decomposers**, and they break down dead organic matter into simpler compounds.
 
• Detritivores play a crucial role in **nutrient cycling, **as they release the nutrients back into the ecosystem for the use of other organisms.
 
• Examples of detritivores include **earthworms, dung beetles, snails**, and some species of** bacteria and fungi.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: What solution should be used to test for the presence of starch in food?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine solution**__.

__
 
• **Iodine solution** is commonly used to test for the presence of starch in food items.
 
• When iodine solution is applied to a substance containing starch, it reacts to form a **blue-black color**, indicating the presence of starch.
 
• The reaction occurs because iodine molecules interact with the helical structure of amylose, a component of starch.
 
• This test is highly specific to starch and does not produce similar reactions with other carbohydrates like glucose or sucrose.
 
• Iodine solution is prepared by dissolving iodine in potassium iodide and water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Starch:**

 
 
• Starch is a polysaccharide composed of glucose units linked together, commonly found in plants.
 
• It is a major source of energy in the human diet, present in foods like potatoes, rice, and wheat.
 
 
 
• **Amylose and Amylopectin:**
 
 
• Starch consists of two components: **amylose** (linear chains) and **amylopectin** (branched chains).
 
• The iodine solution primarily reacts with amylose to produce the blue-black coloration.
 
 
 
• **Iodine Solution Preparation:**
 
 
• Iodine solution is created by dissolving iodine crystals in a potassium iodide solution, which increases iodine's solubility in water.
 
• It is often diluted before use in laboratory experiments.
 
 
 
• **Other Applications of Iodine Solution:**
 
 
• Besides starch testing, iodine solution is used as a disinfectant and antiseptic in medical applications.
 
• It is also employed in titration experiments to determine the concentration of substances in chemistry.

questions.question: What is the primary gas responsible for the leavening effect in bread when yeast ferments sugars?

__
 
• Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is the primary gas responsible for the leavening effect in bread when yeast ferments sugars.
 
• Yeast, a microorganism, consumes the sugars present in the dough and produces carbon dioxide and alcohol as by-products.
 
• The carbon dioxide gas gets trapped within the dough, causing it to expand and rise, resulting in the soft and airy texture of bread.
 
• Besides carbon dioxide, the fermentation process also produces ethanol, but this evaporates during baking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Yeast fermentation is a metabolic process that converts sugar into acids, gases, or alcohol.
 
• Saccharomyces cerevisiae is the most commonly used yeast in bread making.
 
 
 
• **Leavening Agents:**
 
 
• Leavening agents are substances used in dough and batter to produce a foaming action, which lightens and softens the finished product.
 
• Besides yeast, other leavening agents include baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) and baking powder.
 
 
 
• **Proofing:**
 
 
• Proofing is the process of allowing dough to rise before baking.
 
• During proofing, yeast ferments the dough, producing carbon dioxide and causing the dough to expand.
 
 
 
• **Gluten:**
 
 
• Gluten is a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye that gives dough its elasticity.
 
• It helps trap carbon dioxide produced by yeast, aiding in the rising process.

questions.question: Identify a way to reduce the pollution caused due to burning of fossil fuels

options.text: By lowering the temperature of burning
By increasing the efficiency of the combustion process
By increasing the number of carbon molecules

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** Increasing the efficiency of the combustion process can indeed help reduce the pollution caused by burning fossil fuels.** Here are a few ways in which efficiency improvements can be achieved:

 
 
• **Advanced Combustion Technologies:** Utilizing advanced combustion technologies such as pre-combustion chambers, staged combustion, and optimized fuel-air mixing can enhance combustion efficiency. These methods ensure that fuel is burned more completely, reducing the production of pollutants.
 
• **Fuel Quality:** Using higher-quality fuels with lower impurities and better combustion properties can improve combustion efficiency and reduce emissions. This includes using cleaner-burning fuels such as low-sulfur diesel or natural gas instead of coal or heavy oils.
 
• **Cogeneration and Combined Heat and Power (CHP) Systems: **Cogeneration or CHP systems produce both electricity and useful heat from the same energy source. By capturing waste heat from power generation and utilizing it for heating or other industrial processes, these systems improve overall energy efficiency, reducing the need for separate fuel burning and associated emissions.
 
• **Energy Efficiency Measures:** Implementing energy efficiency measures in industrial processes, buildings, and transportation can reduce the overall energy demand. By using energy more efficiently, the need for burning fossil fuels can be minimized, thereby lowering pollution levels.
 
• **Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS):** CCS technologies capture **carbon dioxide (CO2)** emissions from power plants and industrial facilities and store them underground or use them for other purposes. While not directly increasing combustion efficiency, CCS can help reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate the environmental impact of burning fossil fuels.
 
 
 
• It is important to note that while increasing combustion efficiency can reduce pollution per unit of energy generated, it does not eliminate the fundamental environmental concerns associated with the combustion of fossil fuels.
 
• Transitioning to cleaner and renewable energy sources remains crucial for achieving significant reductions in pollution and combating climate change.

questions.question: The percentage of sunlight energy absorbed by the green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem is about ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Only about **1%** of the sunlight energy that reaches the surface of the Earth is absorbed by green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem.
 
• This small fraction is due to the limitations in the efficiency of photosynthesis and the availability of light that plants can utilize.
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.
 
• Most of the sunlight is either reflected by the plant leaves or absorbed as heat, with only a small fraction being used for photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis Process**

 
 
• Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells, where chlorophyll captures light energy.
 
• The process converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen, using the captured light energy.
 
• It is a crucial process for the survival of plants and the production of oxygen for other living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Energy Flow in Ecosystems**
 
 
• Energy flow in ecosystems begins with the absorption of sunlight by producers (green plants).
 
• Only a small fraction of the total sunlight is converted into chemical energy by plants, and this energy is passed through the food chain.
 
• At each trophic level, energy is lost as heat, leading to a decrease in the amount of energy available to higher trophic levels.
 
 
 
• **Light Absorption in Plants**
 
 
• Plant leaves contain pigments like chlorophyll that absorb light primarily in the blue and red wavelengths.
 
• Green light is mostly reflected, which is why plants appear green to our eyes.
 
• The efficiency of light absorption and conversion to chemical energy is limited by various factors, including the intensity and duration of light.
 
 
 
• **Global Primary Production**
 
 
• Primary production is the creation of organic compounds from atmospheric or aquatic carbon dioxide, mainly through photosynthesis.
 
• Terrestrial primary production is a key component of the global carbon cycle, influencing climate and ecosystem dynamics.
 
• The efficiency of primary production varies among different ecosystems and is influenced by factors such as climate, nutrient availability, and plant species.

__
 
• **Meats **is a good source of **vitamin B12**.
 
• This essential vitamin is primarily found in **animal-derived foods**, making meat an important dietary source for individuals following a non-vegetarian diet.
 
• Vitamin B12 plays a crucial role in various bodily functions, including the** formation of red blood cells, DNA synthesis, and nerve function.**
 
• However, for individuals following a vegetarian or vegan diet, other sources of vitamin B12, such as fortified foods or supplements, may be necessary to ensure adequate intake.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vitamin B12,** scientifically known as cobalamin, is a **water-soluble vitamin** that belongs to the group of B vitamins.
 
• It plays a crucial role in metabolism and is essential for various bodily functions.
 
• Animals require vitamin B12 as a **cofactor in DNA synthesis**, as well as in the metabolism of fatty acids and amino acids.
 
• In humans, vitamin B12 is vital for the normal functioning of the nervous system, primarily due to its involvement in the synthesis of myelin. It also contributes to the maturation of red blood cells in the bone marrow, thereby supporting the circulatory system.
 
• Unlike animals, plants do not require cobalamin for their metabolic processes and utilize enzymes that do not rely on it.
 
• Vitamin B12 is distinguished as the most chemically complex among all vitamins. Notably, for humans, it is the only vitamin that must be obtained from animal-derived foods or supplements.

• **G.N. Ramachandran** is renowned for his significant contributions to biochemistry, particularly for elucidating the triple helical structure of collagen.
 
• His work established that collagen, a key structural protein in connective tissues, consists of** three polypeptide chain**s that form a right-handed triple helix.
 
• The discovery of collagen's structure has** implications for medicine**, particularly in understanding diseases related to connective tissues.
 
• Ramachandran's work has earned him recognition as a **pioneer in structural biology,** influencing subsequent research in the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fluid Mosaic Model of a Cell:**

 
 
• Proposed by **Singer and Nicolson in 1972**, this model describes the cell membrane as a dynamic and flexible structure with a mosaic of various proteins floating in or on the fluid lipid bilayer.
 
• It highlights the importance of membrane proteins in functions such as signaling, transport, and maintaining cell shape.
 
 
 
• **Plasma Membrane:**
 
 
• The plasma membrane is the** outer boundary of the cell **that separates its interior from the external environment.
 
• Composed of a lipid bilayer with embedded proteins, it regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell, playing a crucial role in cell communication and homeostasis.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Bodies:**
 
 
• Also known as the **Golgi apparatus**, these organelles are involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• **Discovered by Camillo Golgi in 1898**, the Golgi apparatus is essential for processing molecules synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum.
